LH-REG-002.question: An insurer incorporated in Bermuda wants to sell life insurance policies to residents of Michigan. In Michigan, this company is classified as:
LH-REG-002.explanation: An alien insurer is one organized under the laws of a foreign country, and it needs a Michigan certificate of authority to sell here. A foreign insurer is one incorporated in a different U.S. state, which is the tempting choice but applies only to companies formed within the United States.

LH-PROV-004.explanation: Michigan requires every life policy to give a grace period of 1 month for premiums after the first year, during which the policy stays in force, and lets the insurer deduct the overdue premium from a death claim (MCL 500.4012). Because death occurred within the grace period, the insurer pays $100,000 - $1,200 = $98,800, not the full $100,000.

LH-PROV-008.explanation: Michigan life policies become incontestable after they have been in force for 2 years during the insured's lifetime, except for nonpayment of premium and certain war and disability provisions (MCL 500.4014). Three years after issue, the insurer cannot contest for misrepresentation or concealment.

LH-HPRV-001.explanation: Michigan requires a grace period of at least 10 days for monthly premiums, 7 days for weekly and 31 days for other modes (MCL 500.3410), so coverage continues through June 11 and any unpaid premium can be deducted from a claim. A 7-day grace period applies only to weekly premiums.
